label: Mid-original input of e/w/u/t-type letter in sequences starting with 3/l/i/2
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at positions t=3..6 (t=3-5 hold ~92% of mass); never at t<2, at the delimiter, or during copying. Within that window it acts like a conjunction of graded factors: the current input token (strongest for e, then w, then u/t, weaker for a/k/c) and the sequence first token (strongest for 3 and l, then i, 2, p, h). It mostly fires on the first occurrence of the input token. Peak activations are e or w at t=3-4 in sequences starting with 3 or l; adding first-token conditions raises precision from 0.22 to 0.75 but costs recall. The tail is diffuse low-magnitude firing on other letters, so a boolean predicate reaches only about 0.5 F1 (dev).
